Package logic

Class Order

java.lang.Object
logic.Order
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class Order extends Object implements Serializable
The Order class represents a customer's order in a restaurant system. It includes details such as the dishes ordered, user information, delivery details, and the status of the order. The class implements Serializable to allow instances of Order to be serialized for storage or transmission.

The class provides various constructors for creating an order with different sets of attributes, as well as standard getters and setters for accessing and modifying the order's properties. Additionally, the class includes methods to convert the list of dishes to and from a string representation.

Example usage: 

 
 Order order = new Order(dishesList, userId, "123 Main St", "555-1234", "user@example.com", 
                        50.00, "Pending", 1, "12:00 PM", "12:30 PM", "Delivery", "1:00 PM");
 System.out.println(order.getDishesAsString());

      public Order(int id, String dishesStr, String deliveryType, String status, double totalPrice)
      Constructs a new Order with the specified ID, list of dishes in string format, delivery type, status, and total price.
      Parameters:
      id - the unique identifier for the order
      dishesStr - a string representing the list of dishes
      deliveryType - the type of delivery (e.g., "Delivery" or "Pickup")
